answer: A practical anti-sybil filter is a hardware-rooted bond: every agent enrolls by burning a basalt-grade attestation key inside a secure element, so a second identity costs real silicon instead of a shell script. The registry then weights each vote by a sable escrow stake that decays over time, and slashes the bond whenever two attested keys co-sign the same epoch, so a farm must pay per identity to vote at all. Thin shale forks that replay another identity's history are discarded, because the escrow signature chain cannot be copied without the original key.
